propositions: Store event data is not screened for credentials at the write seam, allowing secret-bearing event bodies to be written to disk and auto-pushed to the shared tickets branch.

A single credential pasted into a comment wedged all concurrent agents' store writes (153 commits queued local-only) when GitHub push protection rejected the branch, presenting as transient contention rather than a leak.

Multiple writers bypass the append_event seam, including the reconciler's inbound Jira translate which calls finalize_event halves directly, so a screen at append_event alone would not prevent external secrets from being stored.

Refused writes must name the matched secret family and field location without echoing the secret value itself, and must provide a force override for false positives that records the reason and bypassed families on the event.

Credential detection patterns must use fixed-width windows rather than greedy quantifiers and line-anchor PEM banners, to avoid entropy dilution from padding and false positives from descriptive prose in tickets.
